description:
🚀 Solo builder from Kanjirappally, India, taking on the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge at NASA Space Apps 2026. 🌍

I designed, coded and presented Mars Base Simulator: Explore · Build · Survive, a game where players land on Mars, mine resources, grow their crew and survive sandstorms and oxygen emergencies. 🛠️🌪️

🎯 My goal is to make real mission trade-offs fun and easy for young learners, and to inspire the next generation of explorers. 🌟
summary:
🚀 Mars Base Simulator: Explore · Build · Survive 🔴
We built an interactive Mars outpost game for the “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer” challenge. 👨‍🚀
🌍 Explore: Land on Mars with a crew of 10 and zero resources, then push through three sectors, each unlocked by another rocket landing.
🛠️ Build: Mine resources and invest them in habitats, a water tower, a greenhouse, a hospital, housing, a radio link, rover production and meteor defense. Every build grows your crew.
🌪️ Survive: Sandstorms burn resources, oxygen alerts cost lives, and a damaged rocket needs repairs. Players quickly learn that air, water, food and protection come before expansion. 💨
🎯 Why it matters: Kids learn systems thinking best by making real decisions with real consequences. Our game turns life support, power, food and protection into hands-on choices, not lectures. 🧠
💻 Built in PenguinMod, a block-based editor, so students can read, remix and extend it. 🌟
details:
🚀 What it does and how it works

Mars Base Simulator is a click-to-play survival game. Players land on Mars with a crew of 10 and zero resources, then mine (+3 resources per click) and spend what they earn on modules: habitats, a water tower, a greenhouse, a supply room, a hospital, housing, a shelter, a radio link, rover production and meteor defense. 🛠️

The mission runs through three sectors (A-1 Lost Signal, A-2 Habitat Zone, A-3 Expansion Zone), each unlocked by landing another rocket. A live HUD tracks Level, Resources, Population and a Countdown to the next sandstorm. ⏱️

Hazards push back. 🌪️ A sandstorm burns 60 resources, an oxygen alert costs a crew member, and a damaged rocket arrives after the repair bay is built. The finale needs power, mission command and meteor defense together.

🎯 Benefits and intended impact

Players feel the trade-offs behind a real outpost: life support, power, food and protection. Housing is the cheapest way to grow the crew, while shelter and radome buy safety, so players learn that spending is a strategy choice. 🧠 We hope it inspires young learners to see space habitats as engineered systems and want to explore STEM careers. 🌟

💻 Tools used

  • PenguinMod, a Scratch-based block coding editor, with 39 sprites, 33 broadcast events and about 870 code blocks
  • Vector (SVG) art for sprites and sector backdrops
  • Sound effects and background music
  • Custom key art for the title and presentation

✨ What makes it creative

Our tagline is the game loop: Explore · Build · Survive. Hazards are tied to engineering lessons, such as the oxygen alert firing as the water tower goes up. The sci-fi HUD styling makes a block-coded project feel like a cinematic mission. 🎬

🧩 Factors we considered

  • Age-appropriate: simple clicks, with no complex controls
  • Balanced economy: costs ramp up so each decision matters
  • Accessible: block code that students can read, remix and extend
  • Alignment: matched to the challenge’s life support, power, food and protection themes
